premise: Writing portions of a fantasy manuscript in Edinburgh cafes while dealing with extreme financial hardship.
hook: She wrote her first blockbuster manuscript in public cafes simply because it was warmer than her unheated apartment.
key_facts: Lived as a single mother relying on state benefits in Edinburgh, Scotland.
Completed the first manuscript of the fantasy novel over several years during her daughter's nap times.
Rejected by a dozen publishing houses before Bloomsbury accepted the manuscript in 1996.
The book went on to launch one of the most successful literary and cinematic franchises in history.

premise: Deciding to make the World Wide Web open-source and free for everyone instead of commercializing it.
hook: He could have become the richest man on earth by patenting the World Wide Web, but he chose to give it away for free.
key_facts: Invented the World Wide Web while working at CERN in 1989
Wrote the first web browser and web server software
Persuaded CERN to make the underlying technology available on a royalty-free basis
Founded the World Wide Web Consortium to guide the open development of the web

premise: Moving from partitioned Poland to Paris to study physics, where a chance meeting in a laboratory led to a historic scientific partnership.
hook: She moved to Paris unable to afford proper meals, subsisting mostly on tea and bread until a laboratory space assignment changed physics forever.
key_facts: Educated in the clandestine 'Flying University' in Warsaw before moving to Paris
Studied physics and mathematics at the Sorbonne while facing extreme poverty
Met Pierre Curie while looking for laboratory space to study magnetic properties of steels
Discovered the elements polonium and radium and won two Nobel Prizes in different sciences

premise: The night a Soviet military officer made the split-second decision to ignore computer warning systems signaling an incoming US nuclear attack, preventing a global catastrophe.
hook: One man's gut feeling stopped a nuclear war in 1983.
key_facts: Served as a lieutenant colonel in the Soviet Air Defense Forces.
Oversaw the early-warning system for missile attacks on September 26, 1983.
Computers erroneously reported that the US had launched intercontinental ballistic missiles.
Decided the signal was a false alarm based on the low number of missiles detected.
